ðŸŒ¡ï¸ TEMPERATURE â€” DEFINITION: Temperature is the average kinetic energy of all molecules present in a body. It tells you the DIRECTION heat will flow (hot â†’ cold). Measured using a thermometer. SI unit: kelvin (K).

ðŸ”¥ HEAT â€” DEFINITION: Heat is the SUM (total) of the kinetic energy of all molecules of a substance. It is a form of energy, measured in joules. Heat flows from a body at higher temperature to one at lower temperature until equilibrium is reached.

ðŸ’¡ KEY CONCEPTUAL DIFFERENCE (exam favorite): Temperature is an AVERAGE (intensive property â€” doesn't depend on amount of substance). Heat is a TOTAL/SUM (extensive property â€” depends on mass/amount). This is why a bucket of lukewarm water can contain MORE heat than a cup of boiling tea, even though its temperature is lower â€” more molecules means a bigger total, even if each molecule individually has less average energy.

âš¡ EFFECTS OF HEAT: When heat is applied to a body, it can bring: (i) Change in temperature (ii) Change in volume (iii) Change of state of matter (iv) Electric effect (v) Generation of light energy (vi) Change in resistance.
âš–ï¸ THERMAL EQUILIBRIUM: Two bodies are in thermal equilibrium when NO heat flows from one to the other after being brought into contact â€” meaning they are at the same temperature.

ðŸ“ ZEROTH LAW OF THERMODYNAMICS: If two systems are separately in thermal equilibrium with a third system, then they must also be in thermal equilibrium with each other. (This law is what actually justifies using a thermometer â€” the thermometer is the 'third system'.)
ðŸ§ª THERMODYNAMIC SYSTEM: A system that can be described using thermodynamic parameters â€” Temperature, Pressure, Volume, and Heat exchange.
ðŸ”¬ THERMOMETRY: The science of temperature and its measurement. THREE MAIN STEPS: (i) Construction (ii) Calibration (iii) Sensitiveness.
